payload.task: Li-ion self_diffusion (cm2/s) in pristine crystalline LiF by molecular dynamics
payload.reason: PREMISE CHECK FAILED. (1) Ill-posed for a pristine crystal: in defect-free rock-salt LiF below melting, Li+ only vibrates about lattice sites; measurable Li diffusion in LiF is vacancy-mediated (thermal Schottky pairs or extrinsic/impurity vacancies), so it depends on defect concentration, which a pristine cell sets to zero by construction. (2) Not measurable at MD scale: equilibrium vacancy fractions in the solid are far below 1/N_atoms for any affordable cell (1e3-1e4 atoms), and vacancy hops are rare events on ns timescales. A perfect-cell MLIP MD run would give a plateaued MSD and 'D ~ 0 within resolution'. That number is an artifact of cell size and run length, not a property of LiF. Getting a nonzero D would need near/above-melting temperatures (superheating or melting, i.e. a different phase) or unphysical defect concentrations. (3) No temperature was specified, and D is strongly Arrhenius. (4) Validation not possible: /data/calibration/tier1.json has no LiF or ionic-conductor diffusion reference, so no independent known result can be recovered with this setup. Running anyway would produce an unvalidated, misleading number, so no simulation was run. WELL-POSED ALTERNATIVES (need a temperature and a measured reference before trusting any result): (a) vacancy-mediated D: compute the Li-vacancy migration barrier (NEB) and Schottky formation energy with the same MLIP, giving D(T) = f a^2 nu c_v(T) exp(-Em/kT), or MD of a supercell with one explicit Li vacancy (+ compensating F vacancy) at specified T, rescaled by the physical vacancy fraction; validate against measured LiF tracer-diffusion or ionic-conductivity Arrhenius data. (b) Li self-diffusion in molten LiF above its melting point, a well-defined MD observable; validate first by recovering LiF's measured melting point or liquid density with the same model.
